findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/material-code-policy.ts:491 preflightMaterialCodeExclusions (the claimed second enforcement layer for excludePaths) is never called by resolveMaterialCodePolicy (lines 305-384) or by any handler/gate — grep across packages/main/src confirms its ONLY caller is the smoke test (packages/main/src/tasks/language-neutral-gates-smoke.ts:301,305), and there it is invoked directly with a hand-fabricated trackedFiles array, not derived from a real git tree at the resolved projectRoot. In real usage, resolveMaterialCodePolicy(dirRoot) for materialCode.excludePaths=["backend/"] does NOT throw (confirmed live: baseName("backend/")=="" so isImmutableManifestName never matches) — the smoke test itself even comments "backend/ passes basename resolve" before manually calling the isolated preflight function. So a project can save an excludePaths entry that covers a real manifest (e.g. backend/ over backend/go.mod) with NO error/warning at config-resolve time, contradicting: (1) the module docstring lines 13-17 ("enforced both at config-resolve time and by a filesystem-aware transition preflight"), (2) config.ts:58-59 MaterialCodeConfig docstring ("via the filesystem-aware preflight, covering"), and (3) checklist.json CHK-002 adversarial verificationEvidence ("rejected at BOTH layers"). Net classification correctness is still preserved for backend/go.mod itself because classifyMaterialCodePath checks the immutable-manifest step (step 1) before excludePaths (step 3) regardless of this preflight, but the promised REJECTION/error-surfacing behavior for misleading directory-level excludes never fires in production — the two-layer enforcement architecture the story claims is DONE is actually one layer.

doc-promise-undelivered: ProofStoryDiagnosticInput.materialClassification (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:144, consumed at proofstory.ts:710 via materialClassificationHasMaterialCode) is NEVER populated by any real production caller. Grep for materialClassification across packages/main/src shows it only appears in proofstory.ts (def+use), review-assurance-floor.ts (a DIFFERENT field on EvaluateReviewAssuranceFloorArgs), and the smoke test. All 5 real diagnosticInput/proofStoryDiagnosticInput builders that feed evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics in production — packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:129, packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts:110 (used by proofStoryDevGateFailure, the actual DEV-gate enforce path), packages/main/src/handlers/proofstory.ts:92, and packages/main/src/handlers/story-review.ts:229 and :733 — construct the ProofStoryDiagnosticInput object WITHOUT a materialClassification field and never call buildMaterialClassificationSnapshot. So in production, materialClassificationHasMaterialCode(input.materialClassification) always receives undefined and always returns false; the new `materialCodePresent` behavior-change signal at proofstory.ts:710 can never fire for real ProofStory evaluations. Only packages/main/src/tasks/language-neutral-gates-smoke.ts:146-170 (helper proofStoryInput()) and :210-211 manually construct an input WITH a hand-built snapshot to exercise this branch — that is not equivalent to production wiring. This directly contradicts checklist.json CHK-001 (marked done): the context text ("ProofStoryDiagnosticInput gains a materialClassification field consumed by the trigger predicate"), the userSees claim ("An identical bug story flips required=true across floor + repro + ProofStory triggers, all driven by one classification snapshot"), and the CHK-001:happy verificationEvidence note pointing at the RED harness (tmp/w1-red/red-language-degradation.cjs), which — confirmed by reading it — only calls classifyReviewAssuranceFloorPath and never exercises the repro-first or ProofStory trigger flag at all. A pure-.go/.py/.rs bug story therefore still does NOT flip ProofStory's red-evidence trigger in real usage; only the review-assurance floor classifier (and, independently, the repro-first gate via its own freshly-built snapshot in evaluateStoryEvidenceBindingGate) are genuinely wired end-to-end.
